messages:
Arjun Bose: heads-up — ml-eval-bot just flagged a quality regression on the int8 bring-up for xlingo-3b-int8. Multilang detok suite shows BLEU/chrF drops and some funky detok around fullwidth punctuation and RTL markers.

ml-eval-bot: automated regression alert: model=xlingo-3b-int8 suite=multilang-detok delta_bleu=-3.4 delta_chrf=-5.2 failing=14/120 samples :rotating_light:

Maya Chen: ouch. can you paste a tiny repro?

Arjun Bose: minimal repro below (original -> ref -> output). note the stray newline before a Japanese fullstop and RLMs appearing around Arabic fragments inside Japanese text.

```
INPUT: 日本語の説明と العربية の混在テキスト。
REF: 日本語の説明と العربية の混在テキスト。
OUTPUT (xlingo-3b-int8): 日本語の説明と
。‏ العربية ‏の混在テキスト。
```

Arjun Bose: tokenizer trace suggests subtoken boundary shifts when the quantized kernel uses the qfusion decode path — merge scoring changes cause a token split before the fullwidth punctuation, decoding emits a newline then the punctuation as a separate token, and we also get surrounding RLM inserted (looks like bidi heuristics triggered on the Arabic subtokens).

Li Wei: does fp16 or q4_0 reproduce?

Arjun Bose: fp16 matches ref. q4_0 has a tiny chrF delta but no newline/RLM issue. int8 is the outlier.

Samir Patel: could be two things: 1) quantized logits perturb beam ranking so a different subtokenization path is preferred at decode time, 2) detokenizer normalization is sensitive to token boundaries and inserts control chars for bidi segments.

Maya Chen: can you run with --bpe-debug and also dump detok steps? small log would help.

Arjun Bose: running now: `python eval_harness.py --model xlingo-3b-int8 --suite multilang-detok --bpe-debug --dump-detok > /tmp/int8_detok.log`

(Minutes later)

Arjun Bose: excerpt from bpe debug: "merge step: candidate="。" split_score=-0.23; alt_split_score=-0.19; chosen=split". Then detok stage: "normalize: attach_space=False; is_fullwidth= True; bidi_wrap=maybe; insert_rtl_marker=True".

Li Wei: interesting — the scores are close. quant noise could flip the decision. If the merge_score threshold is tuned on fp16, int8 rounding might push some merges into split.

Samir Patel: agree. quick experiment idea: replay logits from fp16 and int8 at decode time (fix seed) and compare top-k merge decisions. If fp16 logits produce the same merges as fp16 decode, then the issue is upstream in quant kernels. If logits differ a lot then we know where to bisect.

Maya Chen: also check token IDs around punctuation for any non-canonical unicode normalization — e.g., NFKC vs NFC differences showing up after quantized token selection.

Arjun Bose: plan: 1) dump decode-time merge scores + token ids for a handful of failing samples, 2) replay decode with fp16 logits on int8 model code path, 3) run detok with forced no-bidi-wrapping to see if that hides the RLM. I'll post logs here.

ml-eval-bot: note: created ticket ML-9876 for int8 detok regression, linked to perf/quantization epic.

Maya Chen: thanks. :eyes: if you find it's purely scoring flips we should add a small hysteresis to merge scoring or retrain the merge ranking table for int8 path. if it's detok, patch detok to avoid inserting RLM unless absolutely necessary.

Arjun Bose: uploaded initial logs to the ticket and will attach the small repro set. will update once I've got the decode replay results.

Samir Patel: ping me if you need help with the replay harness — I have a script to align logits and tokenization across precisions.

Li Wei: and I'll audit the detok bidi heuristics — maybe an opt-out flag for mixed-script inline segments during evals.

Arjun Bose: thanks all — will follow up in the ticket with concrete diffs. :thumbsup:
